demonstrated: Real ShareRelay fixture rejects replacement after three deliberately small-limit feedback-loss cycles despite all old payloads being consumed; both attachment reconstruction and exact per-event SQLite mirror reproduce it.
Strict platform risk remains saturated after all four bursts were consumed and feedback omitted.
Immediate and finite-cooldown platform policies sustain replacement admissions while old bytes may remain readable; they are separate experimental probes, not integrated kernel policies.
Candidate risk deadlines survive natural hibernation and explicit reset, are not extended by repeated retirement, and do not restore old-generation sending permission.
Some paused peers recover entire 16 MiB bursts after more than ten minutes, whether close was requested or not.
not_established: No physical-release deadline or location of retained bytes; workstation proxy routing and the external forwarding path are not instrumented.
No proof that 30 seconds is physically safer than immediate expiry.
No continuous or per-object memory bound; metrics cover the whole isolate and have missing periodic samples.
No production CLI/browser Cloudflare transfer or resume certification; JOIN/data integration remains pending.
No firewall packet-blackhole experiment; abort mode closes the local TCP socket with SO_LINGER=0.
No unbounded lifetime stress or calibrated abuse-safe production limits; each object has strict experimental run bounds.
interpretation.recommendation: Continue integration with explicit policy-based retirement of admission risk, independent of consumed/settled/physically-released facts; retain bounded live windows, revocation, generation fencing, rate limits and automatic recovery from saturation. Choose the expiry and reconnect-rate budget by measured experience and platform risk, not a claimed buffer TTL.
